You're absolutely right, thank you for the correction! I misspoke.

`git stash` by default only stashes **tracked** changes — files that are already in the index or have been committed before. New files that have never been committed are untracked and get left behind.

So for your situation:
- Use `git stash -u` (or `--include-untracked`) to stash untracked files along with tracked changes
- Use `git stash -a` (or `--all`) to also include ignored files

That explains why your new file was still there after running plain `git stash`. Good catch!
